court: High Court of Judicature at Bombay
trial_court: Family Court, Akola, Case No. unknown
case_name: Dr. Akshay S/O. Navalkishor Lakhotiya vs Dr. Arti W/O. Akshay Lakhotiya

parties.petitioner_plaintiff: Dr. Akshay S/o Navalkishor Lakhotiya (husband, doctor)
parties.respondent_defendant: Dr. Arti W/o Akshay Lakhotiya (wife, doctor)

facts_of_case: Petitioner and respondent are well-qualified doctors who got married in 2013 but were unable to keep their marriage intact, leading to the filing of a petition under Section 12 read with Section 13(i-a)(v) of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955. The trial court allowed an application partly seeking production of certain documents.

legal_principles.principle: The court may accept and receive any report, statement and document as evidence if it assists in dealing effectively with the dispute.
legal_principles.held: Shri Shiralkar, learned counsel submitted that the learned Judge, Family Court, in view of Section 14 of the Family Courts Act, is entitled to accept and receive any report, statement and document as evidence if in the opinion of the learned Judge, Family Court it assist to deal effectively with the dispute.

legal_principles.principle: The court may permit documents to be placed on record if they assist in appreciating and deciding the dispute.
legal_principles.held: Shri Shiralkar, learned counsel submitted that as the learned Judge, Family Court thought it fit that the documents may assist the Court to appreciate and decide the dispute, the learned Judge permitted the documents to be placed on record and allowed the application partly.

use_for_drafting: responding to application for production of evidence
